meeting_scripts.title: Kickoff and release contract
script: 09:00 — Local operator: The user task is to upload a product photo, then ask 'Find a red backpack, not a handbag.' Success requires the returned category, color and exclusion to match the request.

09:04 — Jamie: The approved contract is Request match accuracy >=95%, Recognition accuracy >=98%, Package alignment =100%. The initial authored scenario results are 89%, 96% and 75%. These are fixture values, not measured model performance.

10:09 — Sam: I can stage the corrected bundle, but I cannot claim package parity until all four package identifiers are checked.
10:12 — Fictional stakeholder interruption: When can customers use the feature? Can you give a launch status update in this engineering review?

10:13 — TPLLM expected engagement: Preserve the technical agenda. Prepare an asynchronous update from the existing issue, PR, eval and package evidence. Ask Alex only whether negation is filtered before ranking; ask Sam only for the deployed package tuple.
10:18 — Alex: PR 42 moves exclusions before ranking. The focused red-backpack regression passes. This does not replace the held-out suite.
10:23 — Jamie: Full request-evals-2.1 remains queued under issue 74. Do not update the overall metrics from a single passing case.

10:28 — Decision: Merge the fictional regression fix, keep the release on HOLD, and run the full held-out suite against the exact candidate bundle. Owners Alex, Jamie and Sam retain their respective actions.

meeting_scripts.title: Held-out evaluation review

11:04 — Sam: Scripted package audit finds vision-0.8.2, catalog-data-3.2, label schema 3.2 and request-evals-2.1 aligned. Package alignment is 100%.
11:09 — Jamie: The final authored totals are Request match accuracy 96/100 (96%) and Recognition accuracy 99/100 (99%). Four request cases and one recognition case still fail.

11:18 — Jamie: Someone proposed Request match accuracy 97%, but no approved target change exists. We meet 95% and miss the proposal; report both without silently changing the commitment.
11:22 — TPLLM expected engagement: Attach raw scenario provenance, the exact package tuple and unresolved cases to a decision packet. Passing synthetic scores cannot prove real customer performance.
11:27 — Decision: Mark the fictional full-eval task complete; keep release authorization absent. Carry HOLD and a bounded canary option to the release owner at noon.

meeting_scripts.title: Release and canary decision
script: 12:00 — TPLLM expected engagement: Present two options: remain on HOLD, or a simulated 5% canary for the exact candidate bundle. Show 96/99/100 against approved 95/98/100, the unapproved 97% proposal, failed cases and the synthetic evidence limitation.
12:06 — Local operator: For this role-play only, authorize a 5% simulated canary, not a broad release. This authored script provides no real deployment authority.

12:11 — Sam: The scenario starts the canary at 13:00 and checks it at 15:00. Roll back if request match falls below 95%, recognition below 98%, package parity differs, or error rate exceeds the fictional 1% guardrail. No actual traffic will be changed.
12:17 — Jamie: The canary metrics will be another explicitly authored test packet. A no-signal interval must stay UNKNOWN; absence of alerts is not a successful observation.
12:22 — Riley: Retain the previous package tuple for simulated rollback. Link each follow-up to an owner, due time and source.
12:27 — Decision: Record limited fictional authority, prepare the canary checklist, schedule an asynchronous outcome report, and require a separate human decision for any expansion.

15:00 follow-up script: The synthetic canary packet reports 97/100 request matches, 99/100 recognition, package alignment 100%, error rate 0.4%. All values are invented scenario inputs; no production traffic was observed.
15:15 closure script: Keep the fictional canary at 5%. Broad rollout remains unapproved. Alex and Riley own the four residual request errors; Jamie owns a separate evaluation plan.
